proof_attempt_summary: D0 developed a same-class lower construction and a clipped threshold scan with a localized fourth-moment argument for atomic designs. D0.5 stopped at novelty triage: the delivered known-design benchmark was graded subfield below the fixed field floor. The math panel did not finish repair of two findings, so the theorem package remains unverified and must not be cited as established.
tldr: In a symmetric binary-response benchmark with a known control regression, known source and target covariate laws, a known positive source propensity, and public shell parameters, the all-learner minimax target-welfare regret is unconditionally \(M_n(\alpha,\delta,\gamma)\asymp n^{-(1+\alpha)/(2+\alpha+\delta+\gamma)}\). The lower bound ranges over every measurable randomized threshold learner and uses explicit full source causal laws together with their observed consistency pushforwards; the same class is attained by a finite clipped product-weight threshold scan with a public offset. The fourth-moment localization theorem is valid for atomic and nonatomic designs, including boundary thresholds and unrestricted target tie mass, so the matched frontier is log free. The accompanying ninety-percent quantity is only a public deterministic worst-case Markov bound, not an empirical uncertainty certificate.
gap: Transported treatment-rule papers establish consistency, efficient value estimation, or generic regret bounds, while transfer-classification and covariate-shift bandit papers quantify different objectives and model classes. The inspected literature does not give a same-class static threshold-policy theorem when target near ties, source covariate scarcity, and treated-arm scarcity coincide and target tie mass is unrestricted.
